actions.description: Capture a single image from a named camera with a declared resolution and exposure and return an image artifact reference.

inputs.description: Camera selector; this package serves one configured camera, so the value is accepted and does not change the connection
inputs.name: camera

actions.name: capture

adjusts.description: Exposure time in milliseconds; the next capture applies it
adjusts.name: exposure_time

facts.text: BaslerCamera is an ophyd Device (basler_camera.py:21) whose components are image, mean, exposure_time, user_defined_name, camera_model, serial_number, image_shape, pixel_level_min, pixel_level_max, active_format, payload_size and grab_timeout
exposure_time is a config Signal whose source comment states the unit is milliseconds

The constructor enumerates pylon devices, creates and opens a pylon.InstantCamera, reads the user-defined name, model, serial number, shape, pixel levels, pixel format and payload size, sets the trigger mode and pixel format, and closes the camera
set_custom_images configures the pylon emulated camera from an image array or an image directory
grab_image starts grabbing one frame, retrieves it with grab_timeout, raises when GrabSucceeded is false, stops grabbing and returns the pylon array
trigger calls grab_image, writes the frame into the HDF5 dataset, publishes the datum id and the frame mean

stage creates the HDF5 resource and dataset, opens the camera, and writes ExposureTimeAbs (1e3 times exposure_time) only when that value lies within ExposureTimeAbs.Min..Max; a value outside is replaced in the exposure_time Signal by the minimum or maximum with a warning and is not written in that call
stage opens a new HDF5 file with mode 'x' at root_dir/YYYY/MM/DD/<uid>.h5 and creates its image dataset with a first frame filled with NaN
The upstream test fixture creates the dated directory tree under /tmp/basler with make_dir_tree
unstage closes the pylon camera and the HDF5 file
The verbose output labels the grab_timeout value in milliseconds
The module imports pylon from pypylon at import time
available_devices enumerates the pylon transport layer's devices
ExternalFileReference is an ophyd Signal that describes an image stored in an external file

operator_required.name: exposure_time
operator_required.reason: the clone states the exposure is in milliseconds (basler_camera.py:24) but no numeric range: the stage applies ExposureTimeAbs.Min/Max queried from the connected camera and clamps the request (basler_camera.py:237-263), so the site supplies the range of its camera

safe_state.description: camera_object.StopGrabbing, the call grab_image itself makes after a frame, is sent to end a running pylon grab; the capture's finally block unstages, which closes the camera, and outside a capture the upstream leaves the camera closed. An imaging sensor with no actuator: the stop proves no physical state; its effect while RetrieveResult waits or on a closed camera is pylon behaviour outside the clone
